correctness.rationale: For any odd p, the five cubic reduction factorization types have counts (\(p^3\)-p)/3, p(\(p^2\)-p)/2, binom(p,3), p(p-1), p summing to \(p^3\). Simple Hensel roots contribute 0,1,3. A double root uses uniform quadratic discriminant divisible by p and has conditional 0,p,2p counts with evaluated probabilities \(Q_p\). A triple root expands to pC+\(p^2\) Bv and has conditional 0,p,\(p^2\) counts with evaluated probabilities \(T_p\). The pgf follows by total probability; symbolic moment algebra gives stated fourth moment. Direct exhaustive integer enumeration of 3^9 and 5^9 monic cubics gives exact matching histograms. The \(p=3\) collision is handled at pgf level; \(p=2\) is excluded.

originality.rationale: The evaluated full seven-level root-count law for uniformly random monic cubics modulo odd prime cubes is not stated in inspected primary sources. Existing highly relevant results either study algorithmic lifting, only finite-ring expectations, full p-adic roots, or all-degree/high-degree related moments. value.rationale: For the natural smallest nontrivial mixed simple/double/triple Hensel branch model, the theorem determines the entire finite-ring root-count law, its sharp rare \(p^2\)-root event (probability \(p^{-5}\)) and the fourth moment growing cubically in p. It answers a structured arithmetic statistics question not implied by merely knowing the mean or the Qp-root law; it supplies a useful exact benchmark for singular modular root lifting. No downstream algorithmic speedup is asserted.
